about: CHAIN tiel_1020 (Design/content/CHAINS.md; page Design/content/chains/tiel_1020.md; words Data/writing/chain_tiel_1020.json). The merchants of Tiel after the lost battle at Vlaardingen (29 July 1018), as the monk Alpert describes them about 1021-1024: they judge their own cases, swear each other clear of debts, keep a common chest and drink together; and they say the emperor gave them a charter for it, which nobody has seen. A seat among them, and what it costs. Fourteen cards, August 1018 to 1030. Tiel is not yet in ports_793.json, so the cards told at Tiel open at Noviomagus, a morning's drift up the Waal (see 'needs' in the page). Step flags ch_tiel_1020_1 .. _10; side flags _witnessed, _asked, _london, _count, _told, _informed, _fair, _silent, _perjured, _settled, _stood, _kept_out, _amends, _claim, _cologne_friend, _paid_in, _charter_plan, _toll_plan, _charter_won, _charter_fair, _charter_lost, _company, _spoke_well, _claim_heard, _bishop; lasting costs _shut_out, _counts_dog; endings ch_tiel_1020_end_seat, _end_guest, _end_charter, _end_bishop, _end_count, and ch_tiel_1020_done; history changed: changed_tiel_charter_1020, changed_tiel_toll_peace. An option's outcome text is the writing key named in its note.

cards.note: Step 1, the start (drawn at Noviomagus, Traiectum, Daventre or Colonia from August 1018 to 1022). An English wool seller asks a Tiel man for a debt; the Tiel man swears it away with his fellows swearing beside him. Source: Alpert of Metz, De diversitate temporum II.20: a Tiel man who has borrowed denies it and swears at once, and a thing that can be hidden in one hand is sworn away with the other (from memory, our rendering (?)); English trade of Tiel (Alpert II.20-21; lowlands_saxony.md). People: Wigbold (Wig- + -bold) and Saewine (Sae- + -wine) are invented. Sets ch_tiel_1020_1, and _witnessed or _asked.

cards.intention: On the bank an Englishman asks a Tiel merchant for the price of twelve sacks of wool. The Tiel man holds up a closed fist and swears he owes nothing. Six men of Tiel swear with him.

cards.note: Step 2 (Noviomagus, 20 days after step 1, standing for Tiel; also drawn). The bench at Tiel at first light: the terms of a seat. Source: Alpert II.20: they give themselves to drinking from early morning, and the man who tells foul stories in the loudest voice to make the common people laugh is most praised; they pool money and feast on it at set times (from memory (?)). The terms (two to swear for you, a pound of pennies, a clean year) are ours (?). The story told is Exeter riddle 25, the onion (texts_793.json exeter_25_onion; the book is of the later 10th century). People: Sibrand is noviomagus.tiel_merchant; Wigbold as step 1. Sets ch_tiel_1020_2.

cards.note: Step 3 (Lundenwic, 14 days after step 2; also drawn). The Tiel men's man in London and the dues of the emperor's men. Source: the London toll rules called IV Aethelred (about 1000; printed by Liebermann, Gesetze I): the men of the emperor who come in their ships are worthy of good laws as the Londoners are; at Christmas and at Easter they give two grey cloths and one brown, ten pounds of pepper, five pairs of gloves and two kegs of vinegar (from memory (?); also realms/frisia_lotharingia.md under the 1000s). Cnut is king from 1016 (cast.cnut). Aelfric's merchant: texts_793.json aelfric_merchant. People: Everwin (Ever- + -win) is invented. Sets ch_tiel_1020_3, and _london if he is helped.

cards.note: Step 4, optional (drawn at Traiectum, Noviomagus, Daventre or Medemelacha after step 2, 1018 to 1025; it tells what happened at the river mouth on the way in, because Flardinga is not yet a port). Count Dirk's steward buys ears. Source: Dirk III built a fort at Vlaardingen and took toll of all who went down to the sea; the Tiel men complained that they could no longer go to Britain nor the Britons come to them, and that the emperor's tolls would fail; the army sent against him was cut down among the ditches on 29 July 1018 and the toll stood (Alpert II.20-21; Thietmar VIII (?); chronicle_793.json 1018-07-29-vlaardingen). That the count bought word of the bench is ours (?). People: Meinward (Mein- + -ward) is invented. Sets ch_tiel_1020_4, and _count or _told.

cards.note: Step 5, optional (drawn at Traiectum after step 2, 1019 to 1024). The monk Alpert asks what the Tiel men do. Source: Alpert of Metz wrote De diversitate temporum, on the years 990 to 1021, and dedicated it to Bishop Burchard of Worms; he also wrote the miracles of Saint Walburg at Tiel; he died in or after 1024 (en and nl Wikipedia, 'Alpert of Metz', read 6 Oct 2026). Where he lived is not known: the diocese of Utrecht, perhaps the abbey of Hohorst (?). His chapter II.20 must rest on somebody's telling: here it may be the player's. That the chest buries the drowned and feeds widows is ours (?), after the alms, fire and wreck agreements allowed in 779 (Herstal c. 16). People: Alpert is historical. Sets ch_tiel_1020_5, and _informed, _fair or _silent.

cards.intention: A monk waits by your boat with a tablet and a stylus. He has heard you drink at Tiel, and he asks his questions like a man who has already written the answers.

cards.note: Step 6, the turn (Noviomagus for Tiel, 60 days after step 2; also drawn once any of steps 3 to 5 is done). A Cologne wine seller sues Wigbold for nine casks unpaid; the bench will swear him clear and asks the newcomer to be one of the hands. Source: Alpert II.20: they judge not by law but by their own will; a borrower denies and swears at once, and perjury is held as nothing (from memory (?)); Tiel's close tie to Cologne is in the digs (lowlands_saxony.md). Seven hands to an oath is the common number of oath-helpers, not Alpert's (?). People: Wezelo, a short Rhenish name of the 11th century (?), is invented. Sets ch_tiel_1020_6, and _perjured, _settled, _stood or _kept_out.

cards.note: Step 8 (Noviomagus for Tiel, in the winter after step 6: November to February). The common chest is opened: the newcomer's pound, and what the year's gain should buy. Source: Alpert II.20: they put money together, share it out among themselves for gain, and from it pay for feasts at set times of the year, and on the high feasts they give themselves to drunkenness as if it were a solemn duty; and they say the emperor handed down and confirmed their way of judging by a charter (from memory (?)). No such charter survives. Henry II dies on 13 July 1024, so the charter can only be asked for until 1023. The pound of entry and the vote are ours (?). Sets ch_tiel_1020_8, and _paid_in, _charter_plan or _toll_plan.

options.note: outcome: chain_tiel_1020.s08.out_charter_success / out_charter_failure (likely; the hard road: laughed down, the pound is still paid in)

cards.note: Step 9, the hard road only (Noviomagus, 60 days after step 8, until June 1024). The emperor's chaplain asks what exactly is to be written. Source: Alpert's 'they say' a charter of the emperor confirms their judging (II.20); none is known. A king's charter was drawn by a chaplain of the chancery, asked for through a bishop or a great man, and paid for with a gift (?); Henry II kept Easter at Nijmegen in 1018 and died on 13 July 1024; that he was at Nijmegen again in these years is likely and unchecked (?). Merchants with a king's writing: Otto II for Magdeburg, 975 (DD O II 112). People: the chaplain is invented and unnamed; Sibrand as before. Sets ch_tiel_1020_9, and _charter_won (with _charter_fair) or _charter_lost.

cards.note: Step 10 (Traiectum, 120 days after step 8 or 60 after a lost charter; also drawn; not for a house that won the charter). Bishop Adalbold asks the merchants who trade at Tiel how debts are sworn away there. Source: Adalbold II, bishop of Utrecht 1010 to 27 November 1026; he stood with the Tiel men against Dirk in 1018 and fled to the ships at Vlaardingen (Alpert II.21; realms/frisia_lotharingia.json); in 1026 King Conrad gave the bishop the count's rights in Teisterbant, the land of Tiel (wp nl Sticht Utrecht). Alpert's book went to Burchard of Worms, whose Decretum has a book on perjury (book XII (?)). The bishop's asking is ours (?). Sets ch_tiel_1020_10, and _company (with _spoke_well), _claim_heard or _bishop.

cards.note: Ending 1, what happened (Noviomagus for Tiel, 40 days after step 10, to 1030; for a house that did not go to the bishop or the count and won no charter). The bench goes on as Alpert describes it: its own judgement, its chest, its cup, and a charter nobody has seen. Source: Alpert II.20; the bishop of Utrecht holds the count's rights in Teisterbant from 1026. A sworn brother's standing (his oath backed by all, a share of the common gain) is what Alpert describes from outside; the keeper of a key and the London store are ours (?). Sets ch_tiel_1020_end_seat (or ch_tiel_1020_end_guest for the man who stays a guest) and ch_tiel_1020_done, with unlock_title_tiel_sworn_brother, unlock_factor_lundenwic or unlock_pilot_waal.

cards.note: Ending 4 (drawn at Traiectum, Noviomagus, Daventre or Medemelacha after step 8, to 1030, for the house that took the count's tally and did not go to the bishop; it tells a call at the count's fort at the river mouth). Count Dirk III pays his man. Source: Dirk III, count in West Frisia 993 to 27 May 1039, kept his fort and his toll after 1018 and the emperor let it be (Alpert II.21; wp nl Slag bij Vlaardingen); the round fort on its mound (lowlands_saxony.md, Flardinga). A fixed yearly sum in place of the toll is not recorded: it is history changed (?). The sands of the Merwede are learned from the men who watch them. Sets ch_tiel_1020_end_count and ch_tiel_1020_done, with unlock_pilot_merwede and unlock_title_count_dirks_man or (the hard road) unlock_title_tiel_sworn_brother and changed_tiel_toll_peace; lasting cost ch_tiel_1020_counts_dog.

cards.intention: On your way in, at the mouth, the steward did not come aboard. He waved you to the creek under the round fort, and the count himself came down the mound to look at your boat.
